title: Cut a cable tie off a cable bundle without nicking the cables
instruction: Cut the cable tie off the cable bundle with the flush cutters from the tray, without nicking any cable's insulation. Then put the cutters back on the tray's rests, leave the bundle across its blocks with nothing holding it, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Technicians cut cable ties off wiring looms, harnesses and network bundles every day. A careless snip nicks the insulation, which can later short or shock someone. The safe way is to hold the bundle still and cut the strap right beside the tie's head, where it stands off the cables.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. Two beech blocks (6 x 5 cm, 5 cm tall) stand 30 cm forward, one 12 cm left and one 16 cm right of the centre line. Across them lies a bundle of seven PVC-insulated copper cables (7 mm each, coloured; 2.1 cm across, 38 cm long, 120 g), running left to right. A black nylon cable tie (4 mm wide strap) is round the bundle 4 cm right of the centre line, between the blocks, its head (7 x 6 x 6 mm) on the near side of the bundle, 30 degrees up from level. A grey ABS tray (18 x 10 cm, 2.5 cm walls) lies 16 cm forward and 25 cm right of the centre line, with two dark rubber rests across it. On the rests lie flush cutters with steel jaws and red PVC-sleeved handles, their jaws pointing forward. The cutters are two steel halves on a pivot (60 g each, 13.4 cm long); the handles are 2.9 cm apart where a hand holds them, 5 cm behind the pivot (about 3.5 cm above the table), and a spring holds the jaws 8 mm open at the tips. Squeezing the handles together closes the jaws; closed 10 degrees, they cut whatever is between the tips. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Severed: the jaws close (10 degrees) with the strap truly between the blades: the strap's middle within 3 mm of the mouth's middle line across the strap (so all 4 mm of its width lies between the 8 mm-apart edges), the jaws' tips no more than 10.9 mm from the bundle's axis (at or past the strap's inner face, 10.5 mm from it), the cutters pointing into the bundle (within 50 degrees) and their pivot axis within 50 degrees of the strap's run; the strap then springs open and the tie falls off. Off the bundle: the cut tie's middle at least 1.5 cm below the bundle's axis or 3 cm from it. 0.0 if a cable was ever nicked: the jaws closed on the strap more than 12 mm (along it) from the middle of its head, where it lies tight on the insulation, or closed with a corner of a jaw's tip pressed 1.5 mm or more into any cable. Otherwise 1.0: severed beside its head and off the bundle, both halves of the cutters back on the tray's rests (within 3 cm of where they lay), the bundle still across its blocks (its middle within 2.5 cm of its line and not below the blocks' tops), each gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) at least 4 cm from the cutters' handles and from the bundle above its left block, and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: severed beside its head and off the bundle; 0.25: the cutters lifted 2 cm out of the tray at some point; else 0.0. In a real trial the tie counts only if its strap is cut through and it has come off the bundle, and every cable's insulation is inspected afterwards: any nick or cut in it scores 0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the cutters and the bundle still.
reset_notes: Put a new tie round the bundle at the same place, its head on the near side, lay the bundle back across the blocks and the cutters back in the tray.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the bundle is one rigid body with the tie glued to it, its strap 0.7 mm off the insulation all round (a real strap stands off only beside its head). Cutting is a rule: when the jaws close with the strap between the blades, the task file swaps the tie for an open one that falls off. A nick is judged from where the jaws closed and how deep the tips pressed, not simulated. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
